cards.q: What does the MPLS lab configure and verify?
cards.a: It configures LDP on the core, verifies label bindings and FIB entries, and builds an L3VPN with MP-BGP, tying IGP, LDP, and BGP together on the provider edge.

cards.q: What is the MPLS core setup sequence?
cards.a: Build an OSPF core, enable mpls ip and LDP, verify labels, then build the VPN.

cards.q: What commands check LDP sessions, bindings, and installed labels?
cards.a: show mpls ldp neighbor, show mpls ldp bindings, and show mpls forwarding.

cards.q: What does mpls ip on an interface do?
cards.a: It enables LDP label distribution on that interface; alternatively mpls ldp autoconfig under OSPF enables it across the core.

cards.q: What is the L3VPN build sequence?
cards.a: Define a VRF, assign VRF interfaces, configure MP-BGP vpnv4, set the rd and rt, then advertise routes.
A VRF combined with MP-BGP vpnv4, carrying VPNv4 routes with their labels.

cards.q: How are labels distributed in an MPLS VPN and what does MP-BGP carry?
cards.a: LDP distributes the transport labels while MP-BGP carries both the VPN labels and VPNv4 routes.

cards.q: What is the MPLS label stack in an L3VPN?
cards.a: Two labels: the first is the transport label from LDP, and the second is the VPN label from BGP.

cards.q: What are PHP, implicit null, and explicit null in MPLS?
cards.a: PHP pops the label, implicit null means pop-only, and explicit null means keep the label (do not pop at the penultimate hop).

cards.q: What commands verify LDP, FIB, VRF, and VPNv4 state?
cards.a: show mpls ldp neighbor, show mpls forwarding, show ip vrf, show bgp vpnv4 (or show bgp vpnv4 unicast), and show ip vrf detail.

cards.q: What configuration creates a VRF and its route-target?
cards.a: vrf definition CUST, then rd 65000:100 and route-target both 65000:100 under the VRF.

cards.q: How is a VPNv4 neighbor activated and communities exchanged?
cards.a: Under router bgp, use address-family vpnv4, then neighbor 10.0.0.2 activate and neighbor 10.0.0.2 send-community both.

cards.q: What is the role of the route-target in MP-BGP?
cards.a: The route-target controls import/export between VRFs (inter-VRF connectivity) and its exchange requires send-community.

cards.q: No LDP labels are being distributed. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: LDP protocol or interface configuration issue, so check show mpls ldp bindings.

cards.q: A VRF remains empty of routes. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An MP-BGP VPNv4 activation or RD/RT mismatch, so check show bgp vpnv4 and the VRF detail.

cards.q: Which single protocol handles both transport and VPN labels in MPLS?
cards.a: None — LDP distributes transport labels while MP-BGP distributes the VPN labels; both are required.

cards.q: mpls ip under router ospf is sufficient; interfaces need no additional label configuration.
cards.a: False — mpls ldp autoconfig under OSPF enables LDP, but mpls ip must be applied on interfaces to enable LDP label distribution (shown as an alternate method).

cards.q: A VPN route does not import into the VRF. What should you verify?
cards.a: The RD and RT match and that send-community is enabled, since route-targets rely on community exchange.

cards.q: What is the recommended MPLS VPN verification order?
cards.a: Verify LDP, then FIB, then VPNv4 — LDP, FIB, VPNv4.
